# Appeal of Denial — Total Knee Replacement (CPT 27447)

**Taylor Kimura**
Member ID: W381271109
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Blue Shield of California
Attn: Member Services Grievances
P.O. Box 5588
El Dorado Hills, CA 95762-0011

**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-25**
**Reference number:** POC-972F74519C-71410
**Member:** Taylor Kimura | **Member ID:** W381271109
**Service denied:** Total knee replacement, CPT 27447
**Governing policy:** *Knee Arthroplasty for Adults* — https://www.blueshieldca.com/content/dam/bsca/en/provider/docs/2023/November/PRV_KneeArthroplasty_Adult.pdf
**Appeal deadline:** This appeal must be received by 2027-02-21.

---

## Why I am writing

I am appealing the denial of the prior authorization request for my total knee replacement (CPT 27447), which Blue Shield of California denied in a notice dated 2026-08-25. The notice states the reason as the imaging findings submitted not supporting the medical necessity of the requested procedure.

I am asking Blue Shield of California to reconsider that decision. The plan's own policy, *Knee Arthroplasty for Adults*, sets out the criteria for this surgery, and the records already in my file address them — including the imaging. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is needed and submitted the request on that basis. Below I have set the plan's own language side by side with what my records show.

---

## The plan's criteria and what my records document

### 1. Radiographic evidence

The policy states:

> "Radiographic evidence of severe osteoarthritis as evidenced by either of the following:"

and lists, as those alternatives:

> "The presence of definite joint space narrowing with sclerosis and possible deformity of bone ends"

> "The presence of large osteophytes, marked narrowing of joint space, severe sclerosis and definite deformity of the proximal tibia or distal femur"

Because the policy says **either** of these will do, meeting one is enough.

My imaging of 2026-06-25 consists of weight-bearing knee radiographs. The report documents bone-on-bone apposition in the medial and patellofemoral compartments, with lateral joint-space narrowing, and grades the findings as Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4. Bone-on-bone apposition is joint space narrowing at its most advanced — there is no remaining space in those two compartments — and the narrowing is present in a third compartment as well.

The denial notice does not tell me which of the two radiographic alternatives above was applied, what the reviewer found lacking in the report, or what additional radiographic finding the plan expected to see. I am asking Blue Shield to identify that specifically on reconsideration. If a particular descriptive finding was expected and is simply not spelled out in the wording of the radiology report, I ask that the films and report be re-reviewed by an orthopedic reviewer rather than the request being closed on the report's phrasing.

I also note that the policy asks for:

> "Radiology report(s) (i.e., MRI, CT) used to make surgical decision"

The imaging my surgeon used to make the surgical decision is the weight-bearing radiograph study of 2026-06-25, and that report was submitted. If the plan requires a different imaging modality in a case like mine, I ask that it say so plainly, and cite the provision that requires it, so that I can respond.

### 2. Diagnosis

The policy states:

> "The reason for the arthroplasty is osteoarthritis (OA), rheumatoid arthritis, osteonecrosis, or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee joint"

My surgery is being done for osteoarthritis of the knee, graded Kellgren-Lawrence 4 on the 2026-06-25 weight-bearing radiographs, with varus alignment on examination. This is the first condition on the plan's list.

### 3. Conservative (non-surgical) treatment

The policy states:

> "Documentation of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management), or documentation of rationale if conservative therapy is considered inappropriate"

and adds:

> "As medically indicated, members with osteoarthritis, traumatic arthritis, rheumatoid arthritis or osteonecrosis should have non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record, including all of the following, unless contraindicated:"

with the items given to me including:

> "Supervised physical therapy which could include an instructed home exercise program, including flexibility and muscle-strengthening exercises."

> "Assistive device use (required for persons with certain relative contraindications to joint replacement, optional for others)"

The policy also asks for:

> "Prior conservative treatments, duration, and response"

My record documents all of this:

| Plan's requirement | What my records show |
|---|---|
| Supervised physical therapy, including strengthening and range-of-motion work | Supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion; 14 weeks, 2026-04-28 to 2026-08-04; 18 visits completed; recorded in the physical therapy discharge note |
| Prior treatments, duration, and response | NSAIDs for 4 months, with inadequate relief; corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-04, giving 3 weeks of partial relief; symptoms of 14 months' duration, progressive, and unrelieved by rest |
| Assistive device use — "optional for others" | The policy makes this optional except for persons with certain relative contraindications. My record documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and non-smoking status. |

On the plan's own wording, conservative therapy here was tried and was unsuccessful: therapy was completed, medication gave inadequate relief, and the injection gave only three weeks of partial relief while the pain has continued to progress.

The policy also states:

> "Individuals with relative contraindications should exhaust all appropriate nonsurgical treatment options prior to surgical consideration."

My records do not identify a relative contraindication, and the denial notice does not assert one.

### 4. Physical examination

The policy states:

> "Documentation of limited range of motion, antalgic gait, and pain in knee joint with passive range of motion on physical examination"

My examination documents limited range of motion of 5 to 100 degrees — I cannot fully straighten or fully bend the knee — along with varus alignment, crepitus, and effusion. Dr. Okafor's complete examination notes are in my chart, and I ask that they be reviewed in full for each element the plan lists here.

### 5. Pain and functional disability

The policy asks for:

> "Clinical records indicating pain and functional disability that interferes with ADLs"

My records document that I cannot climb stairs without assistance and that I wake 3 to 4 times a night because of the pain. The pain has been progressive over 14 months and is not relieved by rest. Stairs and sleep are daily activities, and both are now limited.

---

## One note on the policy language I have

I have quoted the plan's criteria exactly as they appear in *Knee Arthroplasty for Adults*. Several of the provisions I have quoted introduce lists, and the policy contains further conditions and list items beyond the text reproduced above — for example, the excerpt referencing "Failure of a previous proximal tibial or distal femoral osteotomy 4. Hemophilic arthroplasty 5. Limb salvage for malignancy 6. Posttraumatic knee joint destruction" and "Distal femur fracture repair in a individual with osteoporosis" are part of a longer list I have not seen in full. I have not stated any numeric threshold — a required number of weeks of therapy, a minimum grade, or a specific radiographic measurement — as the plan's requirement, because the policy text I have does not state one. If the denial rests on a threshold of that kind, I ask that Blue Shield identify the exact provision it applied so I can address it directly.

---

## What I am asking for

I am asking Blue Shield of California to:

1. Overturn the denial dated 2026-08-25 (reference POC-972F74519C-71410) and authorize total knee replacement, CPT 27447;
2. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician reviewer with orthopedic surgery expertise who has the 2026-06-25 weight-bearing radiograph report and images, the physical therapy discharge note, and Dr. Okafor's clinical notes in hand; and
3. If the denial is upheld in any part, provide me with a written statement identifying the specific criterion in *Knee Arthroplasty for Adults* that my records do not meet, and what documentation would satisfy it.

I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day period stated in my denial notice; it must be received by **2027-02-21**. I understand I may file online using the member grievance form at blueshieldca.com (logging in pre-fills the form), by mail to Blue Shield of California, Attn: Member Services Grievances, P.O. Box 5588, El Dorado Hills, CA 95762-0011, or by phone at 1-800-393-6130 (TTY 711).

Please contact me at the phone number or email above if anything further is needed. I would rather send an additional record than have this decided on an incomplete file.

Thank you for reconsidering this decision.

Sincerely,

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
**Taylor Kimura**
